label: Mid-sequence new tokens after an early h/1/j/0 (original phase and <DEL>)
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read in, plus the <DEL> step (88% of mass in the original phase, 11% at <DEL>, ~1% during copy). It peaks at steps 3-6, never fires at t=0 and almost never at t=1. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (90% of mass). Rate depends on what the current token is (o 4.3x, a 2.9x, f 2.5x, p 2.0x, u/g ~1.6x) and on which tokens came earlier: h, 1, j and 0 among the first tokens or two steps back each give about 3x lift, while z, l, k, y and 2 give less. The strongest activations are o/a/f arriving after a prefix like h h 0 or 1 h j. The window t in 2..7 alone covers 97% of mass but has only 12% precision. Requiring an earlier h/1/j/0 plus a first occurrence gives about 0.23 precision and 0.75 mass recall on dev. The response looks like a graded mix of current-token and prefix-token identity that a clean predicate cannot capture, so precision stays low. Does not fire during copy-phase outputs or on repeated tokens.
